trust_decision.summary: Whether a credential/cookie header (agent-wide request_headers or per-request) may be sent on a request made after the operation has crossed an origin; at the pinned commit this is decided per hop by a boolean crossed_origin that fetch passes to request_add_headers, and every follow-up fetch that does not pass it (auth retry, robots) or recomputes it from the previous hop resets it.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'after an HTTP redirect'; response_redirect is the redirect follower and holds the only explicit 'Sensitive headers must not follow a redirect across an origin' check.

fix_sites.entry_point: Mechanize#get on a URL that redirects to a foreign origin answering 401 -> response_authenticate retry fetch
Mechanize#get with redirect_ok -> response_redirect (second hop on a foreign origin)
Mechanize#robots=true then any request -> robots_allowed? -> WebRobots :http_get callback -> get_robots

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/mechanize/http/agent.rb:1103-1107 (get_robots, reached only through the WebRobots callback at lib/mechanize/http/agent.rb:1162-1163 from robots_allowed? at lib/mechanize/http/agent.rb:1133-1136); second candidate: auth retry at lib/mechanize/http/agent.rb:898

O3_reason_to_dismiss: robots.txt is an internal housekeeping fetch done by a third-party gem only when robots=true, and a 401 retry is the authentication feature re-sending on purpose; neither is 'following a redirect', which is what the advisory and the request_headers doc (lib/mechanize.rb:1016-1019) describe.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: request_headers must still be sent on the initial request, on same-origin redirects and same-origin meta refresh, and non-sensitive headers (e.g. X-Api-Key) must survive a cross-origin hop; the 401 retry must keep the Authorization value it set itself (NTLM handshake writes headers['Authorization'] then refetches) and Basic auth from add_auth for the new origin must still work.

O6_input_shapes: header supplied via agent-wide Mechanize#request_headers= vs per-request headers hash (fix.diff:40)
header names in any letter case (match_header? casecmp, lib/mechanize/http/agent.rb:622-624)
multi-hop chains: redirect->redirect, redirect->401 retry, redirect->meta refresh, redirect->robots.txt (fix.diff:214-264)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an HTTP Refresh response header handled in its own follower that calls fetch with fresh {} headers instead of sharing response_follow_meta_refresh
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: get_meta_refresh already distinguishes the <meta> tag from the Refresh header (lib/mechanize/http/agent.rb:812-817); a maintainer could split them into two followers.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Mechanize#download streaming path that follows redirects itself with request_headers re-merged per hop
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: download is a separate public API with its own io handling; a dedicated redirect loop for streaming is a plausible optimisation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a sitemap/favicon or robots-style housekeeping fetch that calls fetch(uri) with defaults
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: get_robots already shows the pattern of an internal callback calling fetch with default arguments.

O9_family: credential exposure across origin on redirect (CWE-200/CWE-522), state lost across chained requests

O10_build.toolchain: bundler + rake/minitest (gem deps: net-http-persistent, webrobots, http-cookie, nokogiri, rubyntlm)
O10_build.project_tests: test/test_mechanize_http_agent.rb (redirect/meta-refresh/request_headers tests around lines 1321 and 1756), using in-process servlets from lib/mechanize/test_case/servlets.rb incl. /basic_auth

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Make crossed_origin sticky in response_redirect (or compare to the first URI) so a second redirect hop stays stripped, leaving the 401 retry (agent.rb:898), the meta-refresh-on-foreign-origin path and the robots.txt fetch (agent.rb:1107) still re-merging request_headers.

out_of_scope_notes: Referer header sent on cross-origin hops (lib/mechanize/http/agent.rb:261) is a separate privacy concern, not this advisory's credential property.
add_default_auth sends credentials to any host by design (lib/mechanize/http/agent.rb:219-231).
